Compensation and Benefits Competitive pay based on experiencePaid trainingOpportunities for internal advancement About Us:Here at British Swim School, we are more than just a fun, surface-level swim lesson provider. We strive to make a substantial impact within our communities to combat the tragically high child drowning statistics. We invest in quality team members to teach our lessons with the mindset that we are two schools in one, a survival school first and a learn-to-swim school second. As a result, we can support our mission “to ensure that every person, regardless of age or ability, has the opportunity to become a safe and happy swimmer”. The Position:At British Swim School, we teach fun swim lessons, but that’s not all! We shoot through the water like torpedoes toward our swimmers’ goals! We are a team of fun-loving people that are serious about saving lives and having fun while doing it! Working at British Swim School you will notice that...We look for bright, energetic people, willing to roll up their sleeves, take on new assignments, and juggle many things at once while happily asking, “is that all you’ve got?”In return for your efforts, you’ll have an opportunity to work for a fast-growing, creative, and culture-driven company with a prudent opportunity for growth. You’ll also get to help promote a life-changing learning experience and growing team every day.Being a swim instructor, you will be provided the training to teach swim lessons to children and adults, starting at 3-months old, following the British Swim School aquatics program that is gentle, fun, and progressive. Your Typical Responsibilities:Reports directly to and supports the Aquatics Manager and/or Business Owner(s).Instructs swimming lessons in accordance with British Swim School training and program standards, maintaining certifications throughout employment.Work a flexible schedule that may include evenings (4pm-8pm), weekends (8am- 1pm), and holidays as required by business needs.Work in an environment where noise levels are usually moderate to high and be in the water for the duration of the shift.Minimum Qualifications:High school diploma, equivalent, or in the process of completion.Enthusiastic personality.Comfortable in and around the water. Strong swimming skills are a plus but can be taught and developed!Must maintain certifications throughout the length of employment.Must complete all required British Swim School Aquatics-specific training and testing.Preferred Qualifications:Experience working with children.Swimming experience: Have been on a Swim team, Great! 1-2 years preferred but not required.Customer service skills: 1 year preferredLifeguarding/First Aid/CPR/AED Certification(s) preferred (but can be obtained during training) Compensation: $17.00 - $20.00 per hour Working at British Swim School is more than just a job; it’s a chance to create a lasting impact that could change a child's life.As part of the British Swim School Team, you play a role in your local community, empowering others and sharing your passion. It’s a chance to be part of a fun-loving team of dedicated people who are committed to promoting water safety and a lifelong love of the water.While we teach swimming to people of all ages and abilities, most of our students are preschool and elementary-aged kids. Our instructors should like working with this age group and be good at making parents feel comfortable. It's helpful if you have experience with children or in a child-focused job, but it's not required if you can show the right attitude. jobs.description: Employer: Evidence-Based Associates Expires: 10/19/2026 Licensed Mental Health ProfessionalDenton, TXFull TimeExperienced Candidates MUST be willing and able to:Live locally, within 1 hour of the noted territory. Provide therapy inside the family home as a regular part of the position.Maintain a flexible, non-traditional schedule, including evenings and weekends as needed, based on the availability of the youth and family.Regularly travel throughout the full identified service territory to meet with families and provide services where needed.Position Overview: Do you have a passion for working with children and families? We are looking for compassionate, Licensed Clinical Family Therapist in Denton County who want to empower youth and families by creating strength-based behavior change that will be sustained long after treatment ends. You will receive ongoing training in the Multisystemic Therapy (MST) model as you work with families, youth, their communities, and other key members of their ecology to implement MST as designed. Extensive research has proven the effectiveness of MST. MST therapists do whatever it takes, via close collaboration with all involved, to address the needs of juveniles with criminal offenses, including, in some cases, substance abuse. You will empower families to address challenging and/or problematic behavior and to help youth aged 12 - 17 make life-transforming changes. Treatment progress is made through intensive interventions such as skill building, changing unhelpful family interactions, and increasing social support, to name a few. For more information on Multisystemic Therapy, please watch this video: How Does MST Work? Salary: $56K-$58K based on education, experience, and licensure. General DescriptionUnder direction of the MST Clinical Supervisor and within federal, state and local guidelines, the MST Therapist performs advanced therapeutic work. Work involves providing evidence-based, Multisystemic therapeutic (MST) interventions, with a team approach, for at-risk youth and their families. As an MST Therapist, outside clinical employment is not allowed, and MST must be the only form of clinical employment. Non-clinical employment is allowed in addition to being an MST Therapist.Education, Training, and ExperienceMaster’s degree in psychology, counseling, sociology, social work, or other human services field that meets the requirements of an LMSW, LPC-Associate, LMFT-A and who is under the supervision of a Licensed Professional of Healing Arts (LPHA) Supervisor, as recognized by state of Texas. ---Supervision by an LPHA can be provided by the Center at no cost. One year of counseling experience preferredRequires current licensing from the state of Texas. Upon hire, individuals are required to attend an MST orientation training as well as quarterly booster trainings.Must have and maintain a background and criminal history free from any disqualifying offenses as outlined by the Texas Administrative Code (TAC) and the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC).Must possess and maintain a valid driver’s license and automobile insurance.Individuals with an out-of-state driver’s license must be able to obtain a driver’s license in the state of Texas within thirty (30) days.Successful completion of all position-specific training within thirty (30) days of employment is required.Knowledge, Skills, and AbilitiesKnowledge of family systemic approaches and interventions.Therapy with children and adults using cognitive behavioral techniquesCouples therapy using behavioral-based approachesBehavioral therapy targeting school behavior and academic performanceImplementation of interventions within or between systems in the youth’s natural ecology that affect or influence the behavior of the youth (i.e., family, peer, school, and neighborhood)Collaboration and partnership with community agenciesPrevious work providing in-home or community-based therapy servicesKnowledge of community and government service delivery systems and case management delivery systems; of case guidelines, regulations, and policies; of interviewing techniques; of mental illness and the emotional components of physical illness; of rehabilitation methods; of individual needs associated with disabilities; and of community welfare resources.Skill in interviewing and in conducting individual and family needs assessments.Ability to convey instructions and explanations to clients, families, community stakeholders, and other interested parties, to negotiate available services, and to train others. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.Ability to work in a team environment.Ability to display regular and reliable in-person attendance.Understanding and practice of Trauma Informed Care principles.Essential DutiesThe following list outlines key responsibilities for the position; however, it is not exhaustive and does not encompass all responsibilities. Additional duties may be assigned as needed.Conduct MST assessments including review of referral information, identifying and engaging key participants, identifying systemic strengths and weaknesses, and developing an analysis of the fit of problem behaviors within the ecological context.Engage primary caregivers and other key participants in active change-oriented treatment by identifying and overcoming barriers to engagement.Implement a problem conceptualization, treatment planning, intervention implementation, outcomes review and strategy revision procedure using the MST Analytic Process.Maintain clear and concise documentation of treatment efforts that promote peer and supervisory review and feedback, and that demonstrate compliance with the nine MST Principles and the MST Analytic Process.Ability to engage and collaborate with all relevant systems and key participants within each system, to maintain alignment throughout MST treatment.Provide direct clinical treatment using methods compatible with MST principles and practices.Participate in all MST training, supervision, consultation, and MST Therapist development activities.Conduct a minimum of 2 face-to-face contacts per week with individual clients and their families within a variety of settings, which include client homes, schools, and other community locations as needed.Provide therapeutic services using Multisystemic Therapy.Have face-to-face, (and/or video) contact with client's Legally Authorized Representative, if required and applicable.Develops individual treatment plans; and assesses and reassesses clients’ support systems and available community resources, schools, and/or facilities per the MST guidelines.Ensures that all documentation for services rendered is submitted to the Center within (2) business days.Collaborates on discharges for clients by collaborating with the client, family, interdisciplinary treatment team, and community resources.Clinical therapists within the MST program will comply with all grant and Authority guidelines and regulations for all services rendered to clients.Therapists will record, report and evaluate client progress on Authority's Progress Notes through Electronic Health Record (EHR).All MST Therapists must attend 3 hours of professional development per calendar year that is specific to MST or related to working with adolescents and families. The cost of trainings will be covered by the program.Participates in the Center’s Zero Suicide Initiative.Supports individuals experiencing a crisis by promptly connecting them with appropriate Center programs, such as the Mobile Crisis Outreach Team (MCOT), Psychiatric Triage, Crisis Prevention services, and/or other applicable resources. Ensure seamless coordination to facilitate timely intervention.Remains with individuals, when deemed safe, to provide support and maintain a calm environment until specialized crisis staff or emergency personnel arrive to take over intervention efforts. Adheres to safety protocols to prevent escalation of the crisis situation.Participates in debriefing sessions with the immediate supervisor or designated staff following a crisis event. Collaborate with the team to review the incident, identify lessons learned, and ensure all HHSC guidelines and Center policies are followed.#mst #mstjobs #fft #bsft #incredibleyears #pcit #therapy #therapist #clinician #socialservices #lpc-a #lpca #lcsw #lpc #lmsw #lsw #lcsw #lmft #lmhc #mentalhealthjobs #familytherapy #juvenile #evidencebased #cbt #dbt #multisystemictherapy #ebp #ebm #masterlevel #nowhiring #hiringnow #jobs #clinicaljobs #hiring #careers #childfirst #earlychildhood

You will receive ongoing training in the Multisystemic Therapy (MST) model as you work with families, youth, their communities, and other key members of their ecology to implement MST as designed. MST therapists do whatever it takes, via close collaboration with all involved, to address the needs of juveniles with criminal offenses, including, in some cases, substance abuse. jobs.title: Paraprofessional at The LEAD Center
jobs.description: Employer: The LEAD Center Expires: 10/19/2026 ParaprofessionalThe LEAD Center | Hopewell, VAWant a job where you can make a real difference every day?The LEAD Center is a therapeutic day school where relationships matter, students are known individually, and every team member plays an important role. We are looking for caring, dependable, and energetic paraprofessionals who want to work directly with students with disabilities and be part of a supportive school family.As a paraprofessional at LEAD, you won't just be helping in a classroom—you'll be part of a team that teaches students how to be successful in life. You will build relationships with students, support academic instruction, help students develop independence, and learn how to understand and respond to behavior in meaningful ways.What makes LEAD different?You will know your students.Our classrooms are small, which allows you to build genuine relationships and understand what each student needs to be successful.You will be part of a team.Teachers, paraprofessionals, behavior staff, and administrators work together. You won't be expected to figure everything out on your own.You will learn.No special education experience? That's okay. We provide training in academics, behavior, safety, and other skills you need to be successful.You will make a difference.Some days will be challenging. But you will also get to celebrate the small victories—the new skill, the successful transition, the moment of independence, or the connection with a student that didn't happen before.What will you do?Paraprofessionals at LEAD work closely with teachers and students to:Support individualized academic instruction and classroom activitiesHelp students develop independence and functional life skillsProvide positive behavior support and follow behavior plansBuild positive relationships with studentsAssist with transitions, routines, and daily living needsParticipate in community-based and vocational activities when appropriateCollect basic academic and behavior dataMaintain a safe, structured, and positive classroom environmentWork collaboratively with teachers and the LEAD teamWho are we looking for?We are looking for someone who is:Caring, patient, dependable, and willing to learnComfortable working with students who may have significant academic or behavioral needsPositive and flexible when the day doesn't go exactly as plannedAble to work as part of a teamWilling to receive feedback and continue growingEnergetic and ready to be actively involved with studentsPassionate about helping students become more independent and successfulYou don't have to have all the answers. You do need to care about people, be willing to learn, and believe that what you do matters.About The LEAD CenterThe LEAD Center is an ABA-based therapeutic day school serving public-school students with disabilities ages 5–21 in Central Virginia. We partner with local school divisions to provide individualized academic, behavioral, and functional support for students who require a more individualized level of support than may be available in a traditional school setting.Our mission is simple:To teach people to be successful in life.If you are looking for a job where you can build relationships, grow professionally, laugh, learn, and genuinely make a difference in the life of a student, we would love to meet you.Come see what working at LEAD can feel like.

jobs.title: Special Education Paperwork Manager at St. Croix River Education District
jobs.description: Employer: St. Croix River Education District Expires: 10/19/2026 Temporary Special Education Paperwork Manager. Apply OnlineCategory: SCRED - Certified/Special Education Teacher K-12Date Posted: 9/18/2026Location: St. Croix River Education DistrictDate of Availability: ASAPDate Closing: Open until filled Position Purpose:The Temporary Special Education Paperwork Manager provides specialized support for the development, coordination, and completion of special education due process paperwork for up to 10 young adults, ages 18–22, participating in a transition program. This temporary position is responsible for coordinating and facilitating Individualized Education Program (IEP) and evaluation processes and completing required special education documentation in accordance with state and federal requirements. Responsibilities include facilitating IEP and evaluation meetings, developing IEPs and annual goals, developing evaluation plans, coordinating special education evaluations, completing Evaluation Summary Reports, and ensuring required special education paperwork is completed accurately and within required timelines. This position does not provide direct instruction or direct services to students. The Paperwork Manager works collaboratively with the staff who provide daily instruction and related services, to gather information, review student progress, develop appropriate IEP goals and services, and maintain continuity between the written IEP and the student's educational programming. The position may be performed remotely, with virtual participation in meetings as appropriate. Regular communication and coordination with the transition program team are essential components of the role. Performance Responsibilities:1. Coordinates special education paperwork and due process responsibilities for up to 10 young adults, ages 18–22, participating in a transition program.2. Coordinates and facilitates annual IEP meetings, including communication with required team members, preparation of documentation, facilitation of team discussion, and participation of students, families, and IEP team members.3. Develops compliant IEPs, including present levels, measurable annual goals and objectives, services, accommodations and modifications, progress-monitoring procedures, transition services, and other required components.4. Collaborates with instructional and related service staff to gather student performance data, progress-monitoring information, staff observations, transition data, and family and student input needed to develop and update IEPs.5. Coordinates progress-monitoring requirements, including establishing data collection expectations with staff, reviewing collected data, and completing required progress reports. This position does not provide direct instruction or routinely administer progress-monitoring measures to students.6. Coordinates special education reevaluations, including reviewing existing information, developing evaluation plans, coordinating assessment responsibilities, and obtaining required parent/guardian input and consent.7. Conducts evaluation-related activities that can be completed without direct student contact and within the scope of the individual's professional training and licensure, and collaborates with other qualified professionals completing direct assessments.8. Reviews and synthesizes evaluation information, develops Evaluation Summary Reports in collaboration with multidisciplinary team members, and facilitates evaluation and eligibility determination meetings.9. Completes additional required special education documentation, including Prior Written Notices, IEP amendments, evaluation plans, progress reports, and meeting documentation.10. Monitors special education timelines, maintains accurate student records, and ensures required documents are completed, finalized, distributed, and maintained in accordance with district procedures and applicable requirements.11. Collaborates regularly with instructional staff, related service providers, school psychologists, administrators, families, and other team members to ensure IEPs and transition plans accurately reflect student needs, programming, strengths, preferences, and postsecondary goals. Participates in a monthly transition program team meeting, which may occur virtually.12. Maintains confidentiality, communicates professionally, consults with special education administration regarding complex due process or eligibility questions, and performs related work as assigned. Other Duties as Assigned:Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications:Current Minnesota special education teaching license required.Experience developing Individualized Education Programs, facilitating IEP meetings and completing special education evaluations preferred.Knowledge of Minnesota and federal special education requirements and due process procedures.Knowledge of transition planning and services for students ages 18–22 preferred.Ability to interpret educational, evaluation, and progress-monitoring data and use that information to develop appropriate IEP programming.Strong written communication, organization, collaboration, and time-management skills.Ability to collaborate effectively in a team-based model in which instructional, transition, evaluation, and paperwork responsibilities are shared among multiple professionals. Ability to work effectively in a remote or hybrid environment and maintain consistent communication with program staff, families, and other team members. Work Location and Schedule:This position may be performed remotely. Virtual participation in IEP, evaluation, and team meetings is permitted when appropriate.The employee must be available during mutually agreed-upon school-day hours for required IEP meetings, evaluation meetings, consultation with staff and families, and a monthly transition program team meeting. Other paperwork and documentation responsibilities may be completed on a flexible schedule, consistent with required timelines and team needs. Anticipated Hours Per Week: Up to 10 hours per week Terms of Employment:Temporary PositionAnticipated Duration of Assignment: through June 1, 2027. Evaluation:Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with district procedures for temporary personnel. Application Procedure:Apply online.
